news.Title: Cisco (CSCO) Is Considered a Good Investment by Brokers: Is That True?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Cisco Systems (CSCO).

Cisco currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.80, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 28 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.80 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 28 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and one is Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 57.1% and 3.6% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for CSCO

Check price target & stock forecast for Cisco here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Cisco, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Should You Invest in CSCO?

Looking at the earnings estimate revisions for Cisco, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 1.3% over the past month to $5.17.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Cisco. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for Cisco may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: Ciena's $116M Free Cash Flow: Can Cash Generation Improve in FY27?
news.Content:
Ciena Corporation CIEN generated $116 million in free cash flow during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 despite higher working capital investments to support growing customer demand. Although cash conversion declined sequentially, management highlighted an improvement from the year-ago period. The company's focus on improving operational efficiency, strengthening supply capacity and expanding profitability could support its cash generation prospects over the longer term.

During the third quarter, Ciena increased inventory levels and invested in working capital to support higher revenues. These investments came amid strong business momentum, with third-quarter revenues increasing 37% year over year to $1.67 billion. Adjusted gross margin reached 46.4%, while adjusted operating margin rose to a record 22.5%, more than doubling from the year-ago level. These improvements reflect disciplined cost management, favorable product mix and pricing discipline.

Ciena is also prioritizing capital allocation to support its expanding business. In June, the company issued five-year zero-coupon convertible debt, allowing it to retire its 5.5% interest-bearing term loan and reduce its cost of capital. The transaction also provided funding to secure supply over the next three years. Ciena ended the third quarter with $2.8 billion in cash and equivalents. Management expects fiscal 2026 capital expenditures to reach the higher end of its $250-$275 million projected range.

However, near-term cash generation could face pressure. Management expects cash from operations to decline in the fourth quarter as it makes additional investments under long-term supply agreements extending through 2029.

Looking ahead, Ciena expects fiscal 2027 revenues to increase at least 30% year over year to $8.3-$8.4 billion, with potential upside depending on supply availability. Adjusted gross margin is projected at 45%-46% or higher, while adjusted operating margin is expected between 25% and 27%.

Although management has not provided specific free cash flow guidance for fiscal 2027, the anticipated revenue growth and margin expansion suggest improving underlying cash generation potential. However, continued working capital requirements and supply-related investments could influence the pace of improvement.

Taking a Look at CIEN's Competitors

Cisco Systems CSCO is benefiting from broad demand across networking, security and collaboration. AI infrastructure orders, integrated silicon and an end-of-support refresh opportunity support a multi-year networking cycle, while newer security products and Splunk's recovery broaden the growth base. The company also retains operating leverage and continues to return cash to its shareholders. Cisco ended the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 with $15.9 billion in cash and investments and generated $5.4 billion in operating cash flow, up 27% year over year. The company returned $12.7 billion to its shareholders in fiscal 2026. For fiscal 2027, Cisco projects revenues of $72.2-$73.4 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $5.05-$5.11 per share. Hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenues are expected to reach $7.5 billion, up from approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026.

Story Continues

Arista Networks, Inc. 's ANET sustained investment in AI infrastructure and enterprise upgrades supports demand for its high-speed Ethernet solutions. Rising Etherlink adoption, a broader AI fabric portfolio and expanding campus networking offerings strengthen its long-term growth outlook. ANET's unified software platform and automation capabilities deepen customer engagement across cloud and enterprise networks. For 2027, management projects revenue growth between 38% and 40%, translating to approximately $18.5 billion at the midpoint. ANET's AI fabrics revenues are expected to double to approximately $7 billion, while campus networking revenues are projected to increase 60% to approximately $2 billion.

The earnings report also comes at a pivotal moment for CSCO stock. Shares have recently faced pressure after Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco to "Equal-weight" from "Overweight" and cut its price target to $120 from $135, citing pull-forward risks from planned price increases and potential gross-margin pressure from a growing mix of lower-margin hyperscaler hardware.

With Wall Street still broadly bullish but expectations elevated, Cisco's latest results and management commentary could provide an important catalyst for the stock.

About Cisco Stock

Cisco Systems is a global technology company headquartered in San Jose, California, that develops networking hardware, cybersecurity, collaboration, observability, and AI-driven infrastructure solutions for enterprises, governments, and service providers. The company has evolved from its networking roots into a leading provider of secure connectivity and AI-era digital infrastructure, with a growing focus on software and subscription-based services. Cisco has a market cap of $388.9 billion, making it one of the world's largest technology companies.

Cisco Systems has delivered strong gains over the longer term, but the stock has come under significant pressure ahead of its fiscal first-quarter earnings report on Nov. 12. CSCO has returned 40% over the past year and gained 30% year-to-date (YTD), reflecting investor optimism around the company's growing exposure to AI infrastructure, hyperscale customers, and data center networking. However, the recent trend has been much weaker, with the stock down 15% over the past month as investors have become increasingly concerned about valuation, AI-related gross-margin pressure, and whether strong expectations are already reflected in the share price.

Story Continues

Moreover, the selling intensified last week. Cisco shares slumped 7.6% on Nov. 5 after Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock and reduced its price target to $120 from $135. The firm argued that Cisco's strong rally had reduced the room for further upside and highlighted the risk that customers could pull forward orders ahead of planned price increases. Morgan Stanley also warned that Cisco's growing mix of lower-margin hardware sold to hyperscalers could weigh on gross margins as the company expands its AI infrastructure business. The stock then fell another 2% on Nov. 6, closing at $93.85, before staging a sharp 5.1% rebound on Nov. 9 to $98.65. As of this morning's trading, CSCO has risen almost 3% and is now above the $100 mark.

The rebound suggests that investors may be viewing the recent weakness as an opportunity to reassess Cisco ahead of earnings rather than abandoning the AI-networking story altogether. With the stock still substantially higher over the past year despite its recent pullback, the Nov. 12 earnings report could be critical in determining whether CSCO can resume its upward trend or remains under pressure.

The stock is currently trading at 21.65 times forward earnings, which is a modest discount to industry peers, while in terms of price-to-sales (P/S) of 5.96, the stock seems to be trading at a premium.

Q4 and FY2026 Results Set a High Bar for November Earnings

Cisco delivered a strong finish to fiscal 2026, reporting its fourth-quarter and full-year results on Aug. 12. The networking giant posted record quarterly revenue and earnings, with results exceeding the high end of its previous guidance. Q4 revenue rose 18% year-over-year (YoY) to $17.3 billion, while on a non-GAAP basis, net income increased 23% to $4.9 billion, while adjusted EPS rose 23% to $1.22 from $0.99. Its operating income climbed 38% to $4.3 billion, and the operating margin expanded to 24.7% from 21%. Operating cash flow also increased 27% YoY to $5.4 billion.

The strength was led by Cisco's product business, with product revenue increasing 24%, while services revenue was essentially flat. Networking revenue jumped 28%, Security revenue increased 14%, Collaboration rose 12%, and Observability grew 6%.

Meanwhile, Cisco's Q4 total product orders increased 35% YoY, while networking product orders surged 40%, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. The company also recorded $4 billion of AI infrastructure orders during Q4, bringing full-year AI infrastructure orders to $9.3 billion.

For fiscal 2026, Cisco's revenue increased 12% to $63.3 billion, while non-GAAP net income rose 13% to $17.2 billion, and adjusted EPS increased to $4.33 from $3.81. Full-year networking revenue was particularly impressive, rising 22% to $34.7 billion, while Security grew 2% to $8.2 billion, Collaboration increased 4% to $4.3 billion, and Observability rose 4% to $1.1 billion.

Furthermore, for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, management guided for revenue of $18 billion to $18.2 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.32 to $1.34. For the full fiscal year, Cisco expects revenue of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $5.05 to $5.11. The company also expects $7.5 billion of AI infrastructure revenue in fiscal 2027, nearly double the roughly $4 billion delivered in fiscal 2026.

In addition, analysts are forecasting EPS of around $4.42 for fiscal 2027, a 21.4% YoY jump, and a 8.6% rise to $4.80 in 2028. The consensus EPS estimate of $1.15 for the first quarter of 2027 indicates a 42% rise YoY.

What Do Analysts Expect for CSCO Stock?

In addition to Morgan Stanley taking a neutral stance, Bernstein analyst Peter Weed also recently reiterated a "Hold" rating on CSCO stock with a $110 price target. This reflects Bernstein's cautious stance on CSCO despite the firm's recognition that networking companies stand to benefit from sustained AI infrastructure spending.

On the other hand, on Nov. 3, Bank of America Securities analyst Tal Liani maintained a "Buy" rating on Cisco Systems and a $150 price target ahead of the company's fiscal first-quarter earnings report. The unchanged target reflected the firm's continued bullish view of Cisco's AI-driven networking opportunity and long-term growth prospects.

Overall, CSCO stock has a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 27 analysts covering the stock, 16 advise a "Strong Buy," one suggests a "Moderate Buy," and the remaining 10 analysts are on the sidelines, giving it a "Hold" rating.

CSCO's average analyst price target of $132.79 indicates an upside of 32%, while the Street-high target price of $165 suggests that the stock could rally as much as 64%.

Price and EPS Surprise

With this earnings history in mind, recent estimates have been moving higher for Cisco. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the company is positive, which is a great sign of an earnings beat, especially when you combine this metric with its nice Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Cisco has an Earnings ESP of +1.59% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on November 12, 2026.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Positive Points

Revenue grew 89% year-over-year to $320.7 million, with gross profit turning positive and adjusted EBITDA more than doubling quarter-over-quarter.

AI platform now represents approximately $7.6 billion of expected contracted revenue, including $4.7 billion from the Tydal lease and $2.9 billion of AI cloud backlog.

AI Cloud revenue was $20.4 million, up 46% sequentially and more than 11 times year-over-year, with 4,328 GPUs deployed at approximately 95% utilization.

Negative Points

Net loss was $125.5 million, or $0.46 per share, driven by non-cash items including $125.8 million of depreciation and amortization and a $54.6 million fair value loss on Bitcoin-denominated borrowings.

Cash and cash equivalents declined to $163.7 million from $456.8 million at the end of the second quarter, due to heavy investment in data center construction and land purchases.

Total debt increased to $1.95 billion, up approximately $107 million from the second quarter, reflecting additional Bitcoin-denominated borrowings.

Average power costs rose to $0.07 per kilowatt hour from $0.04 in the second quarter, putting pressure on margins.

Regulatory and permitting uncertainties exist, including potential slowdowns in Norway and the U.S. following midterm elections, which could delay data center approvals and increase community-related costs.

Q & A Highlights

Q : What is the status of Tito project financing for Phase 1, and what are the key milestones for Phase 2? A : CFO Michael Potter said Bitdeer is advancing its project financing plans. Customer Volta reportedly secured its GPU financing, removing the last major item needed to activate the letters of credit. The company believes it is on track for the December 31 Phase 1 milestone and for Phase 2, citing advanced construction, existing grid power from the site's prior Bitcoin mining use, and the strength of the LC backstop.

Q : How are AI cloud customer prepayments evolving, what percentage of CapEx can they fund, and how is the customer mix expected to shift? A : Founder, Chairman and CEO Jihan Wu said prepayments should remain well above 50% of related GPU deployment costs in the near future. He expects prepayment pressure to rise as capital markets tighten for new AI clouds and labs, reducing competition from players willing to build without prepayments. Bitdeer plans to focus on underserved AI labs and AI startups rather than hyperscalers, whose terms he described as less favorable.

Q : Does the current funding mix of Bitcoin sales, AI cloud prepayments and project financing suggest equity financing will be avoided in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027? A : CFO Michael Potter said the company will not rule anything out, but it wound down its ATM program at the end of Q2 and has not recently accessed the equity market. Bitdeer plans to link contracted cash flows to project financing and fund GPUs through large customer prepayments plus shorter-term financing. Equity is intended mainly for earlier-stage investments.

Q : What is the status of the Rockdale site, including interconnection rights, land and the potential transition to AI/HPC? A : CEO Jihan Wu said the acquired land is sufficient to build AI data centers at Rockdale, and the company is seeking additional grid power, with good news possible in the near future. CFO Michael Potter added that the $100 million, 200-acre transaction did not include water rights, but Bitdeer has an arrangement to get water to the site. Bitdeer now controls the interconnection and can transfer power from its existing site to the new site, and it has a formal substation-sharing agreement with SLR.

Q : How should investors think about the regulatory and permitting backdrop for converting U.S. mining sites to AI and HPC after the midterm elections? A : CEO Jihan Wu said the outlook is somewhat uncertain after the midterms, and he expects data center construction to require better arrangements with local communities on taxes and community contributions. He sees higher operating costs as fair, and said already-energized sites have an edge over the next one or two quarters as new approvals slow.

Q : What is the status of the Clarington and Fox Creek sites? A : CFO Michael Potter said there is no update on Clarington, where Bitdeer continues to pursue relief against a lawsuit it believes lacks a good basis; the current plan is Bitcoin mining there. At Fox Creek, the company continues building the power plant, expected in production mid-to-late next year, and has secured gas supplies and made electricity generation more robust for the planned 100-megawatt site.

Q : How is Bitdeer thinking about its global power footprint, including further expansion or selling powered land? A : CFO Michael Potter said Bitdeer is not looking to sell powered land, given scarcity and long-term growth plans, and can generate solid cash flow by mining Bitcoin while sites await AI conversion. He said nothing is absolute if an outsized offer emerged, but the company is comfortable with its position.

Q : How do recent Norwegian restrictions on new data center construction affect Tito and Bitdeer's other Norway site? A : CEO Jihan Wu said he expects everything in Norway to slow down, with fewer permissions and approvals, but it is too early to say data centers cannot be built there. He described AI as a fundamental next industrial revolution that Norway is unlikely to fully forgo.

Q : What is the remaining Tito construction spend, and what size financing is Bitdeer targeting? A : CFO Michael Potter said about $500 million remains to complete Tito construction across Phase 1 and Phase 2, with Phase 1 nearly complete ahead of the December 31 deadline. Bitdeer would seek at least $500 million of financing and aims to pull out more equity than it has put in, subject to market conditions.

A : CEO Jihan Wu said Bitdeer will continue investing in mining expansion but slow the pace of capex next year. Wafer availability is tighter due to strong AI demand. He said script mining, including Zcash, offers higher revenue per megawatt than Bitcoin mining and Bitdeer has an edge in machines for that algorithm, so it will continue to expand there, though competition from new Zcash miner developers is emerging.

Q : Why is Malaysia advantageous for Bitdeer's AI cloud business compared with the U.S.? Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Nov. 10, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Head of Investor Relations - Pretesh Dahya

Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer - Jihan Wu

Chief Strategy Officer - Haris Basit

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Bitdeer Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to hand the conference over to your speaker today, Tesh Dahya, Head of Investor Relations.

Pretesh Dahya: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Bitdeer Technology Group's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Jihan Wu, Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer; Haris Basit, Chief Strategy Officer; and Michael Potter, Chief Financial Officer. Today's call will begin with Haris, who will provide a high-level review of our strategy. Michael will then review our operating highlights and third quarter financial results before we open up the lines for questions. To accompany today's call, we have provided a supplemental investor presentation available on Bitdeer's Investor Relations website under Webcasts and Presentations. Going forward, our infrastructure metrics previously provided in our monthly production updates will be included in our quarterly earnings release.

Before management begins their formal remarks, I would like to remind everyone that during today's call, we may make certain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties, which may cause actual results to differ materially. For a more complete discussion on forward-looking statements and the risks and uncertainties related to Bitdeer's business and industry, please refer to the company's annual report on Form 20-F and other filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. I also want to note that we will be discussing certain non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted EBITDA and adjusted profit or loss and operating metrics today.

A reconciliation of these measures to the most direct comparable GAAP measures is included in our earnings release issued earlier today. These measures should not be considered in isolation from or as a substitute for the most directly comparable GAAP measures. As a reminder, changes in the fair value of our digital assets and certain borrowings are reflected in GAAP net income or loss and may introduce noncash volatility into our reported results. A replay of this call will be available on our Investor Relations website shortly after the call concludes. With that, I will now turn the call over to Haris.

Story Continues

Haris Basit: Thank you, Tesh, and good morning, everyone. The third quarter was an important period in Bitdeer's evolution. We continue to build a diversified technology and digital infrastructure platform with a growing presence in AI Neocloud services and high-performance computing infrastructure. The market continues to evolve quickly. Bitcoin markets remain cyclical. Demand for AI compute continues to outpace available supply, while competition for power, infrastructure and customers is intensifying. Against this backdrop, our advantage is our ability to develop, control and monetize power infrastructure. Power is the foundation of our platform, and we aim to deploy it where it generates the greatest long-term economic value. We do that across two platforms, AI and crypto.

Our AI platform spans AI cloud services and HPC infrastructure. In AI cloud, we deploy GPU capacity alongside customer commitments with disciplined utilization and capital investment. In HPC infrastructure, we develop and lease large-scale data center capacity to credit-supported customers under long-term agreements. The economics are driven by contracted revenue, not Bitcoin prices or GPU markets. Our Tydal project in Norway is a significant milestone as we advance construction toward initial delivery. Our crypto platform spans Bitcoin self-mining and our SEALMINER ASIC design. Self-mining generates revenue from our existing power while providing flexibility as we develop sites for longer-term HPC opportunities. Our proprietary SEALMINER technology gives us control over the efficiency and cost of our mining hardware.

We deploy it across our own facilities and with our co-mining partners. Since both platforms run on a common foundation of power, infrastructure and technical expertise, we gain both schedule and capital flexibility. We can mine to monetize available power today while we develop infrastructure for long-term HPC leases, and we can invest in GPU capacity when and where we see attractive contracted demand. We are beginning to see that strategy translate into long-term revenue visibility. Our AI platform now represents approximately $7.6 billion of expected contracted revenue. That includes approximately $4.7 billion from the base term of our Tydal lease and approximately $2.9 billion of AI cloud backlog. These carry different revenue recognition profiles and capital requirements.

But together, they show the scale of what we are building. Our priorities are clear: deliver Tydal, expand AI, cloud and HPC infrastructure in line with demand, pursue disciplined and financeable growth and keep improving the efficiency of our mining operations. We do not want to depend on any single market cycle. Our objective is to build a platform that generates durable cash flows from the power and technology assets we control. With that, I will turn the call over to Michael.

Michael Potter: Thank you, Haris, and good morning, everyone. The third quarter was a record quarter for Bitdeer. Revenue grew 89% year-over-year to $320.7 million. Gross profit turned positive and adjusted EBITDA more than doubled quarter-over-quarter. Bitcoin mining continues to generate most of our revenue in the near term, while our AI platform scales. Before the details, a quick scorecard against what we told you last quarter. Tydal Phase 1 remains on schedule for delivery at year-end. In Malaysia, A102 is sold out and A201 is more than 70% contracted. Our first GPU financing for A102 is in final stages. All 221 megawatts at Massillon are now online and equity was a much smaller part of our funding.

We raised $58 million under the ATM, a continuation of and compared with $457 million in the second quarter. Our focus is on execution. Let me start with our AI platform, beginning with AI cloud services. AI Cloud revenue was $20.4 million, up 46% from the second quarter. That is more than 11x the $1.8 million we reported in the third quarter of 2025. Our deployed GPU count was roughly flat quarter-over-quarter. The sequential growth came mainly from pricing and mix as utilization of our higher-value GB-class systems increased. Our AI cloud ARR was approximately $86 million at the end of September. We ended the quarter with 4,328 GPUs deployed at approximately 95% utilization.

AI Cloud generated $3.1 million of gross profit in the quarter, a gross margin of approximately 15%. That compares with gross losses of $2.3 million in the second quarter and $0.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. Contracted demand continues to build. During the third quarter, we signed significant multiyear GPU cloud agreements with leading enterprise technology companies. Deliveries of NVIDIA GB300 systems under several of these agreements are expected to begin in November. Malaysia is where most of this demand is landing, and the third quarter was a breakout period for our Malaysia footprint. At our A102 facility, we sold out all 9.5 megawatts ahead of energization.

These five year commitments represent more than $800 million in expected revenue. At A201, we secured offtake commitments for more than 70% of the 21.7 megawatts. That represents more than $1.7 billion in expected revenue over five years. We also ordered more than 100 racks of GB300 systems for the site. We expect revenue to begin at A102 in the first quarter of 2027. A201 will follow in the second quarter of 2027. Together, these commitments lifted our expected AI cloud revenue backlog to approximately $2.9 billion. These contracts carry attractive unit economics. Average over the contract terms, A102 implies approximately $17 million of revenue per megawatt per year and A201, more than $21 million per contracted megawatt.

Revenue in any given year may vary with contract pricing schedules and deployment timings. Once both sites are fully deployed, they represent more than $500 million of annualized revenue. We also added meaningful AI cloud capacity since the end of the second quarter. In September, we signed a 10-year agreement for A202, a 65.1 megawatt facility at our Johor campus. Energization is expected in the third quarter of 2027. In October, we added A901, a 67-megawatt campus expected to be ready for service in the second quarter of 2027. We also signed an eight year agreement for A103, a 60-megawatt Vera Rubin-ready facility at our Cyberjaya campus. Energization is expected in the first quarter of 2028.

Including these sites, our secured AI cloud data center capacity is now approximately 332 IT megawatts. That's about 95% of our 350 IT megawatts target for the first quarter of 2028. I want to be precise about what these numbers mean. Secured capacity means sites we own or hold under an executed data center services agreement. It's not the same as customer contracted capacity. The combined value of our signed AI cloud contracts and AI cloud opportunities under negotiation now exceeds $10 billion. This includes our approximately $2.9 billion backlog. The amount under negotiation is not a binding commitment. Turning now to our HPC infrastructure, the second part of our AI platform. Our focus remains on Tydal.

Tydal is leased to Volta for 16 years, subject to the tenant's no fee termination right at 10 years. The lease covers 121 IT megawatts or 133 gross megawatts. The base term value is approximately $4.7 billion. If the eight year renewal option is exercised, it would rise to approximately $8 billion. Over the base term, average annual revenue, including rent and service fees is approximately $293 million, with an expected NOI margin of about 90%. This implies roughly $264 million of average annual NOI. Tydal is the conversion of one of our existing Bitcoin mining sites to HPC infrastructure. Grid power and much of the electrical infrastructure are already in place.

This significantly reduces the interconnection and energization risk that many new build data center projects face. The site workforce has grown to more than 300 working two shifts. Long lead equipment, including the battery energy storage systems was ordered in advance of requirements. Key electrical equipment has also begun arriving on site. The 22 kV transformer houses and UPS systems are now installed. The battery storage buildings are nearly complete and dry coolers are being mounted. The remaining work is focused on three areas: completing the high-voltage connection to the new data halls, commissioning and integrated systems testing. Phase 1 delivery remains on schedule for year-end. Customer installations are planned to begin in January.

Phase 2 data hall deliveries are expected to begin at the end of the first quarter of 2027. Rent payments for the first eight years are expected to be backed by dedicated credit support. For years 1 to 6, that support is anticipated to be approximately $1.3 billion of irrevocable letters of credit. They are expected to be issued by two highly rated global financial institutions. For years 7 and 8, we anticipate an approximate $475 million dedicated cash reserve. Our portfolio has approximately 3.1 gigawatts of global power capacity with about 1.75 gigawatts online.

Most of our near-term AI capacity is in Norway and Malaysia where the power is secured, and many of our largest U.S. sites are already energized. Turning to our crypto platform, beginning with self-mining. We mined 3,855 Bitcoin in the quarter, up 43% from the second quarter. September was a record month at 1,355 Bitcoin. Self-mining hash rate continued to expand during the quarter. It reached approximately 82.3 exahash per second at quarter end. Co- mining revenue was $59.9 million, up 140% quarter-over-quarter. Co- mining hash rate was 28.7 exahash per second.

Our power cost per Bitcoin mined was approximately $36,000 in the third quarter, in line with the second quarter despite higher average power prices and down from $49,000 a year ago. That reflects continued fleet upgrades, which strengthened our underlying cost position. Our self-mining fleet efficiency reached 15.4 joules per terahash by the end of the third quarter from 20.1 a year ago. As we complete our SEALMINER upgrades, we expect fleet efficiency to continue to improve. Maintaining a leading fleet efficiency position is particularly important during periods of lower Bitcoin prices, helping preserve margins and operating flexibility. On ASIC design, our A4 Ultra Hydro operates at 9.45 joules per terahash at the mining rig level.

We continue to deploy SEALMINER into our own sites and into co-mining partner sites as opportunities arise. Across both platforms, we aim to develop our sites as a good neighbor in partnership with local communities and governments. Our approach is to secure our own power without drawing on existing ratepayers. We pay for the grid infrastructure our facilities require, and we invest locally through jobs, training and long-term partnerships. In September, we signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge that reaffirms our commitment to responsible digital infrastructure development. Now to our financial results. Third quarter revenue was $320.7 million. That is an increase of approximately 89% year-over-year and 40% sequentially. Most of the sequential growth came from self-mining and co-mining.

Self-mining contributed approximately $49 million of the increase and co-mining approximately $35 million. AI Cloud added approximately $6 million. Gross profit was $10.8 million for a gross margin of 3.4%. That is $19.4 million improvement from the second quarter. Higher Bitcoin production, improved fleet efficiency, increased co-mining activity and AI cloud growth drove the gain. These benefits more than offset higher average power costs. Our average power costs rose to $0.047 per kilowatt hour from $0.044 in the second quarter. Turning to operating expenses. G&A declined to $32.8 million from $34.3 million in the second quarter. R&D was $28.2 million compared with $36.1 million in the second quarter, which included a onetime development expense.

Selling expense was $4.2 million, up from $2.2 million, driven by higher advertising and marketing expenses. Interest expense was $34.3 million. Net loss was $125.5 million or $0.46 per share. The result reflected noncash items. These included $125.8 million of depreciation and amortization. They also included a $54.6 million fair value loss in Bitcoin denominated borrowings as Bitcoin prices increased. These were partially offset by a fair value gain on our Norway power purchase agreement. Because we repay our Bitcoin denominated borrowings with mined Bitcoin, the fair value loss on these borrowings is a noncash timing-related impact. Adjusted EBITDA was $69.6 million, up approximately 173% year-over-year and 124% sequentially. That represented an adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.7%.

As a reminder, we transitioned to U.S. GAAP on January 1, 2026, and prior periods have been recast. On that basis, third quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $25.5 million. Sequentially, adjusted EBITDA rose about $38.5 million. revenue grew about $92 million, led by Bitcoin production and co-mining. That was partially offset by about $40 million of additional electricity costs as our expanded fleet consume more power. Other cash costs rose about $14 million. This reflects a larger self-mining fleet, co-mining growth and AI cloud. Moving to the balance sheet. We ended the quarter with $163.7 million of cash and cash equivalents. We also held $50 million of restricted cash.

That compares with $456.8 million of cash and $39.5 million of restricted cash at the end of the second quarter. Digital assets were approximately $43 million and digital assets receivables, mainly collateral for our Bitcoin denominated borrowings was about $344 million. We invested approximately $288 million in data center construction and land, including significant construction spending at Tydal and the land purchase at Rockdale. We also continue to invest in GPU capacity to support AI cloud demand. In total, capital expenditures in the quarter were $478 million, including approximately $110 million for SEALMINER production. We made net repayments of approximately $92 million on our related party loan. Total debt was $1.95 billion, up approximately $107 million from the second quarter.

The increase reflects additional Bitcoin denominated borrowings from BIT, a related party and a higher Bitcoin price. Our convertible notes totaled $1.2 billion in principal. Coupons range from 4% to 5.25%. None mature before December 2029. On liquidity, let me be direct. Cash declined because we funded a heavier investment quarter, including Tydal Construction and the Rockdale land purchase ahead of our expected financing. That was a deliberate choice to protect the construction schedule. Operating cash flow was approximately $6 million. This includes the customer prepayments, but not the $221.5 million of mined Bitcoin we sold, which is reported in investing activities. Together, operations and Bitcoin sales generated roughly $227 million of cash during the quarter.

Our funding plan matches each major use with a dedicated source. First, Tydal. The remaining CapEx of the Volta lease of approximately $350 million is expected to be funded with project level financing, secured by contracted rent. Second, AI cloud GPUs where customer prepayments are our core source. Deferred revenue, mostly AI cloud prepayments rose to approximately $342 million at quarter end. These prepayments fund a large part of the related GPU deployments, 50% or more. Third, our ongoing Bitcoin production, including 1,355 Bitcoin in September, which supports our mining operations and corporate needs. If needed, we can also phase discretionary capital spending such as non-Tydal construction. We're already doing this as I discussed in our outlook.

On financing, we're in the final stages of GPU financing for our 9.5-megawatt A102 site in Malaysia. Work is underway on a similar financing for our 21.7 megawatt A201 site. Some GPU financings may be shorter term, so we pay down that debt faster. Lenders are differentiating sharply by structure and counterparty. We seek to structure our financings around contracted cash flows, customer prepayments and where available, credit support from reputable financial institutions. We have started our own Tydal project financing process, and we'll share updates as appropriate. We prioritize non-dilutive project level financing wherever contracted cash flows can support it.

In the near term, our goals are to close the Tydal project financing, complete the A102 and A201 GP financings and deliver Tydal Phase 1. Finally, our outlook. For 2026, we now expect crypto mining infrastructure capital expenditures to be at or below $200 million, the low end of our prior range of $200 million to $280 million. We're directing capital towards our contracted AI and HPC projects while we complete our financing. Our long-term mining strategy is unchanged. This guidance excludes spending on SEALMINER hardware, GPUs, AI cloud and HPC infrastructure development. Remaining Tydal capital expenditure for the Volta lease of approximately $250 million will be spread across Phase 1 and Phase 2 delivery. That spend extends into 2027.

We expect to provide 2027 capital guidance with our fourth quarter results. We also expect our mining hash rate to continue to grow over time, subject to normal seasonal curtailment. To close, let me step back. The past several months have brought increased volatility. Bitcoin prices moved sharply. Credit is tightened across AI infrastructure, and investors are asking harder questions about how these projects get financed and delivered. Those concerns are understandable. Our model is built for this environment. Our AI and crypto platforms share one power foundation and complement each other. That flexibility matters. We do not have to force every site into one model. We match each asset to the approach that fits it best.

A large, well-connected site may suit a long-term lease, a smaller site with strong customer demand may work better for AI cloud. A site being developed for AI can mine Bitcoin until it is ready. Our objective is simple. Maximize the return on every power asset and protect the balance sheet while we do it. That means funding growth with contracted revenue, customer prepayment and asset level financing wherever we can. We believe this is the right path to durable value for our shareholders. Now our focus is execution, delivering Tydal on schedule and on budget, bringing Malaysia online and closing our financings. Thank you, operator. Please open the call for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Nick Giles with B. Riley Securities.

Nick Giles: Lots of updates here today. I first wanted to ask about the AI cloud business, kind of how you're seeing prepayments evolve? What percentage of CapEx you think you can achieve today? And then if you could just outline kind of your current customer mix and your desire to kind of shift that mix towards -- more towards AI labs with higher rates or more towards hyperscale like parties. Any color on that would be great.

Jihan Wu: I think the prepayment will be well above 50% in the near foreseeable future. And I think the pressure for those demand to pay more in prepayment actually is higher because the capital market is closing the door for all the new labs -- sorry, for all the neocloud. So Basically, the situation is, not any neoclouds or any of our competitors will be able to do any new CapEx without very good support from the client themselves. So which means that we don't have any kind of meaningful competitions that are willing to accept really no prepayment and doing the project.

I think that the neolabs, AI-related startups are very underserved on the market, while frontiers, I think, are a little bit overserved. And hyperscalers' terms are not very good, profitability, I mean. So we think that we will quite focusing on the neolabs and AI startups.

Nick Giles: That's really helpful color. For my follow-up question, I wanted to shift to Rockdale. And I was curious if you could just remind us of the status of that interconnection, whether any approvals by ERCOT would be required for the transition or potential transition to AI. And then you made a recent -- some recent land acquisitions. Do you have any more land around the site that you need to acquire in order to fully leverage the site for HPC?

Jihan Wu: We're still looking into this situation, but I think the land we acquired is already enough for us to carry out our AI transition on the Rockdale site. And I think we want to apply more electricity from the grid, which actually we were hinted or even kind of promised for quite a long time. But we are still waiting. I think in the next year maybe, we can get some more electricity and we can start to build out AI data centers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Nick Cremo with Barclays.

Nikolai Cremo: As we think about converting the existing U.S. mining sites to AI and HPC over time, how should we think about the regulatory and permitting backdrop following the midterm elections? And just having those sites already energized put you in a relatively better position?

Jihan Wu: We do feel a little bit uncertain after the midterm election, but my guess is that the data center constructions will need to have a better arrangement, clear arrangement with the local community on the tax and the community contributions. I think eventually lots of the data centers will still get permission from the local community to go, to start. That's my estimation of the future situation. Which means a little bit higher cost for the data centers to operate in the community, but I think that's fair.

And of course, those data centers that is already running, I think they do enjoy this kind of short-term uncertainty in the next one or two quarters, I guess, because everybody will be slowed down but those data centers already being built or finished have an edge over others.

Nikolai Cremo: Understood. And then for my follow-up, on Tydal, can you just give us an update on the project financing for Phase 1 as you approach year-end delivery? And then more broadly on Phase 2, how should we think about the key milestones and execution priorities as you move towards delivery, I think, in Q1, Q2 next year?

Michael Potter: I think in terms of the financing part, we're advancing on our plans to do the project financing. I think everybody has seen that our customer, Volta to report in the news was out and was successful in securing their GPU financing. And that removed the last major item that needed -- was needed to activate the LC with the remaining part just completing the construction and getting the GPUs working, which is normal for a site like that. Obviously, everything is subject to market conditions and market is relatively tough for any sort of AI financing. But we believe a combination of very short time left for the construction. So the construction is quite advanced.

The fact that the power was on and working for Bitcoin mining before we convert the site to AI. So we don't need to hope that utility will provide the power because it's there already. And the strength of the LC backstop that we have will help us there. In terms of milestones, I mean, we're very close to the December 31 milestone for this year completing Phase 1, and we believe that we're on track. And we also believe that we're on track for Phase 2 as well. Obviously, that was tested by the market somewhat when Volta was out doing the GPU financing. And there was a fair amount of external due diligence that was done then.

So if you're going to take any sort of comfort in our progress, I guess you can take a nod to that.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Colonnese with H.C. Wainwright.

Michael Colonnese: Congrats on all the progress across the platform. First one for me. I'm just curious, how should we expect the AI cloud revenues to ramp throughout 2027 following this accelerated pace of contract execution you've seen in the business as you look to convert this backlog, right? I mean, assuming five-year contracts against $2.9 billion of TCV, by our math, that will equate to about $580 million of ARR. So really the question is, when should we expect it to achieve this full run rate and how we expect those revenues to ramp again as we progress through '27?

Michael Potter: So we're going to provide 2027 guidance with our Q4 2026 earnings release. All of our revenue turns on when the different phases turn on. We've given rough guidance of when we expect energization or delivery. Usually, a few months after that, the GPUs can be up and running, but we'll provide more specific guidance in our Q4 earnings release.

Michael Colonnese: Got it. And to clarify, so it's capital expenditure guidance as well as AI cloud revenue guidance on the 4Q.

Michael Potter: We're going to give 2027 guidance in Q4.

Michael Colonnese: Great. And as a follow-up, if you can just provide a little bit more color on prospective tenant discussions and how those could be progressing at Rockdale following the recent acquisition of additional acreage at the site? And just the dynamics between you deciding whether or not to convert existing Bitcoin mining data center capacity there versus building AI data centers from scratch as you look to utilize capacity at that campus?

Michael Potter: Jihan do you want to answer the question about the customer plans and discussions?

Jihan Wu: In the AI cloud?

Michael Potter: Yes, for Rockdale.

Jihan Wu: Well, Rockdale we have no plans to do really massive winding up of the mining operation and then waiting for a client. Our plan is to use the acquired land and try to get more power from the grid, and then we build a new AI data centers on the new land. So actually, our pressure to get customers is not that big. We can build from small and expanding over the years, and supplying various demand. We are quite flexible on this. So right now, we are quite focusing on getting new power from the grid, which I think we can certainly expect to have good news in the near future.

And -- at the same time, we will design and do lots of the geo work to prepare for the site. I think this kind of resources is quite good for us. So I'm not now very concerned about getting client for the Rockdale.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Todaro with Needham.

John Todaro: Congrats on the progress this quarter. I just want to go back on the CapEx and financing part. You listed out some of the mix on Bitcoin sales, AI cloud prepayment. Does this kind of suggest deliberately that there shouldn't be expected equity financing in Q4 '26 or into Q1 '27?

Michael Potter: I mean we're not going to tie our hands absolutely because you don't know what's going to happen in the world. But the ATM, we wound down sort of at the tail end of Q2 that extended a little bit into Q3, and we haven't been accessing the market for equity recently at all. As we said in our prepared remarks, we do plan on linking contracted cash flows to do more normal project financing and our GPU as a Service, a combination of the large customer prepayments and shorter-term financing. So we're not trying to stretch to the limit over five years.

We believe that will be doable in the market today and provide ample capital for us to execute on our GPU opportunities. Equity financing, we're trying to limit to earlier-stage investments that typically would be funded by equity. And right now, we're concentrating on executing on our revenue opportunities that we've contracted for that are directly in front of us.

John Todaro: Understood. That's appreciated. And then on the Weathersfield, Ohio site, I believe it says you own 40 acres there and that site can go to 300 megawatts. Do you need to buy more acreage there? Or would that be enough to support a 300-megawatt either PSP or cloud data center design?

Jihan Wu: That piece of land right now is in the middle of local communities, kind of a distraction I think. I think we still need more time to get permission from them, if we can. And we have already seen some other local communities approving data centers after a very good community contribution plan. I think we want to do that in the near future. But on the land wise, I do not think that we really need to buy land. We can do a data center with the existing land.

Operator: Our next question comes from Greg Lewis with BTIG.

Gregory Lewis: I had two questions. The first is around the power footprint. I mean, obviously, it's global, it's big. I guess two questions in there. Are there thoughts about -- and hey, we have a lot of pipeline in the existing footprint. But are there thoughts about continued expansion? And then also -- is there also thoughts about subtraction, right? I mean like there's -- the value of land, the value of power has gone up. Are there sites now that maybe the company would think about kind of high grading as they look at positioning the portfolio over the next kind of one, two, three years?

Jihan Wu: Michael, could you answer the question?

Michael Potter: Sure. We're not looking at selling any of our powered land. As you noted, the value for that has gone up, and it's because of scarcity. And we don't think that turning powered land into some short-term gain when we have very long-term plans to keep growing the company. We do have the advantage of a very robust and strong ability to mine Bitcoin with leading ASIC development and the actual miners and in great position. So if we need to wait a little bit until we can actually do an AI data center or something different, we can still generate pretty good cash flow from the sites we have.

So I wouldn't think that we're going to try and turn any of the land we currently have into a short-term gain. Again, nothing is absolute. I guess if the pile cash was big enough and Jihan decided it's the right thing to do, we would consider it. But right now, we're pretty comfortable with our position.

Gregory Lewis: Okay. Great. And then I did want to talk a little bit about Norway. I guess there were some regulations about not a site like Tydal that's already contracted or at least Phase 1 is online. But is there any -- I guess, maybe following that news in Norway where I guess they're putting a hold on new construction. Does that impact, I guess, any later phases at Tydal? And how does that also impact the other site in Norway?

Jihan Wu: Well, we do feel everything will be slowed down in Norway. But I think it's too early to say that the data center will be impossible to build in Norway, because AI is the next industrial revolution. It's a very fundamental element. I don't think Norway will keep up fully. But we do see that everything will be slowing down in the permission, in the approval.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Grondahl with Northland.

Mike Grondahl: Michael, you mentioned something $350 million left at Tydal. Could you just repeat what you said about that? And then do you have a rough range for the financing needed at Tydal? If you could help us with that, that would be great.

Michael Potter: We said we'd be spending about $500 million to complete the construction at Tydal, and that's just a moment in time measurement of what's left to be spent in terms of -- between Phase 1 and Phase 2. Obviously, the activity is relatively heightened. So Phase 1 is very, very close to completion now with us being a couple of weeks in the November and December 31 deadline. So that's just an indication of how much is left to do in terms of the spending, not the actual construction activity, which is quite advanced.

Financing-wise, if we're spending $500 million, we'd want to get at least $500 million, and we've indicated that we're going to be looking to get more financing to pull out some of the equity that we put into the site in the past. The total amount that would be financed is always going to be dependent on market conditions. And when we do go out, what the reception is to our plans. But we do have a plan to take out more than we've put in for resent CapEx.

Mike Grondahl: Got it. And then any update on Fox Creek or Clarington?

Michael Potter: Sorry, go ahead, Jihan.

Jihan Wu: Yes, Michael, please go ahead.

Michael Potter: Yes. No update on Clarington. It's the same status it's been for a while. We continue to pursue relief against the lawsuit that was brought against us that we don't really think has a good basis. And we're currently planning and using it for Bitcoin mining. We believe we can get good value out of that site for Bitcoin mining if we don't do an AI data center there. So our current plan is Bitcoin mining at Clarington. Fox Creek, we continue to build the power plant and it's expected to be in production mid to end of next year. We've done some behind-the-scenes work to secure gas supplies and to make the electricity generation more robust.

So whereas the data center hall was being built for joint use between AI and Bitcoin mining, the power would have been a little bit potentially intermittent for AI, but we've kind of removed that in the background. So we're working to get Fox Creek online, and that will be a 100-megawatt site mid to third quarter of next year.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Kinstlinger with AGP.

Brian Kinstlinger: I'm curious, once it scale, what is the target gross margin and EBITDA margin range for the AI cloud business?

Michael Potter: So we'll talk about the financial targets and the model in a lot more detail when we report the Q4 results. So right now, reaching scale will be happening next year, and it will be part of our guidance for next year.

Brian Kinstlinger: Okay. And then can you speak at a high level to SEALMINER and how you're thinking about production and capital allocation going forward?

Michael Potter: Jihan or Haris, do you want to talk about our SEALMINER?

Jihan Wu: Yeah. We will continue to invest into the expansion of our mining operations. I think next year we will slow down a little bit on the pace of investing new capital, but we will continue to expand our mining operations.

Operator: Our next question comes from Stephen Glagola with KBW.

Stephen Glagola: Haris and Michael, at Rockdale, can you clarify what infrastructure and related rights were transferred to Bitdeer as part of the $100 million transaction for the 200 acres? And specifically, did the purchase include SLR's interconnection rights and water rights and the SLR-owned substation?

Michael Potter: So it didn't include the water rights, but we do have an arrangement to get water to the site as part of the deal, but the water rights themselves were not transferred over. In terms of power, we have control over the interconnection now and the ability to transfer power from our existing site to the new site.

Stephen Glagola: Okay. Great. And did you guys purchase the substation as well?

Michael Potter: We have an agreement to share the substation because the SLR does use a small part of the substation that we mainly use. So it's more formal and with us more in control versus them being in control as our landlord.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our next question comes from Kevin Dede with JonesTrading.

Unknown Analyst: Kind of curious about how you see Malaysia developing. I know that it's been a big focus for your AI cloud business, and I'm wondering if you see Bitdeer in an advantageous position in competing for, I think what you said is underserved AI startups in that region versus other competitors perhaps, and maybe offer a little comparison with how you see that business evolving in the U.S.

Jihan Wu: I think it's quite good for us to be able to expand in Malaysia, especially in this kind of midterm uncertainty in U.S. We will be able to expand our AI cloud business on time without to worry about our own data center construction pace. And right now, most of the U.S. companies, Asian-based tech companies are all looking to Malaysia capacity. Our U.S. sales team get lots of inbound demand inquiries about our capacity in Malaysia. Because right now it's really hard to rent any data centers in United States within next year, RFS.

So I think it's really great that we can lock lots of capacity in Malaysia and continue to lock more and grow the AI cloud there. And while at the same time, our U.S. data centers are being built in DeepLab on the U.S. speed. So we don't need to really worry about whether our AI cloud can grow or not. We can just execute and fulfill the demand from our customers.

Unknown Analyst: I am also curious about wafer allocation from TSMC and your, I guess, your plan to use it. I know last quarter you mentioned Scrypt mining, and I am wondering how you are looking at Zcash and the wafer availability itself and associated pricing.

Jihan Wu: I think our wafer availability is a little bit tight, much tighter than before because of the strong demand from AI. So I think we will slow a little bit on the CapEx on crypto mining business next year. And we have no plan for doing Zcash. And Scrypt mining right now is really good for us because in terms of revenue dollar per megawatt, it's higher than Bitcoin mining, and we will have an edge over other competitors in terms of the mining machines in this algorithm. So we will continue to do more Scrypt mining.

Unknown Analyst: The feedback I have gotten is that Zcash is incredibly profitable and there is very huge shortage of machines given that there only seems to be one manufacturer who you know well.

Jihan Wu: Yeah. But the competition for the Zcash mining, I think, will also be very fierce. Lots of potential new Zcash mining rig developers are already in the market to take out and to order lots of wafers from Samsung and TSMC. So I think to strategically give up Zcash is good for us.

Operator: Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Potter for any closing remarks.

Michael Potter: Thanks, everybody, for joining our call today, and I look forward to talking to you in the future. Thank you.

Operator: This concludes the conference. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell, or Hold Cisco Systems Stock Before Q1 Earnings?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO is set to release its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Cisco Systems expects revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion. Non-GAAP earnings are projected to be in the range of $1.32-$1.34 per share.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues is pegged at $18.09 billion, suggesting 21.54% year-over-year growth. The consensus mark for first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $1.33 per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days and indicates 33% growth over the year-ago quarter's reported figure.

CSCO's earnings surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, the average being 2.55%.

Let's see how things have shaped up prior to this announcement.

Key Factors to Note for CSCO's Q1 Earnings

Cisco Systems' fiscal first-quarter 2027 performance is expected to have benefited from strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, growing hyperscaler investments and continued enterprise network modernization. Increasing adoption of agentic AI is driving demand for high-performance networking solutions across cloud, on-premises and edge environments. Cisco Systems' expanding portfolio of networking, security and observability solutions is expected to have supported revenue growth in the to-be-reported quarter.

AI infrastructure spending by hyperscalers is expected to have remained a major growth driver. Cisco Systems secured $4 billion in hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, bringing full-year orders to $9.3 billion. Growing adoption of Silicon One-based systems, Acacia optics and high-performance networking solutions is likely to have supported revenues. The company's expanding design wins with hyperscalers remain noteworthy.

Enterprise networking demand is expected to have strengthened Cisco Systems' performance. Increasing investments in data center modernization, campus networking and AI-ready infrastructure are likely to have driven demand for switching, routing and wireless solutions. Data center networking orders increased by more than 35% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while campus networking orders grew 20%. Strong adoption of Wi-Fi 7 and next-generation switches is expected to have sustained this momentum.

Cisco Systems' security business is expected to have benefited from increasing cybersecurity spending and growing adoption of its integrated security offerings. Rising demand for Secure Access, XDR, Hypershield, AI Defense and firewall solutions is likely to have supported growth. Strengthening Splunk adoption and integration with Cisco Systems' broader security portfolio are additional positives. Management anticipates mid-to-high-single-digit security revenue growth in the to-be-reported quarter.

However, Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 performance is expected to have faced pressure from rising memory costs and a higher mix of lower-margin hardware revenues, potentially weighing on gross margins. The company is also suffering from stiff competition from Arista Networks ANET, Dell Technologies DELL and Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE across AI networking and enterprise security domains.

Story Continues

CSCO Shares Outperform Sector

Cisco Systems' shares have appreciated 28.1% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's return of 4.1%.

However, CSCO's shares have underperformed Arista Networks, Dell Technologies and Hewlett-Packard Enterprise YTD. Shares of Dell Technologies, Arista Networks and Hewlett-Packard have appreciated 175.1%, 42.1% and 98%, respectively.

The Value Score of F suggests a stretched valuation for Cisco at this moment.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, CSCO is trading at 5.3X, higher than the broader sector's 4.84X, Dell Technologies' 0.99X and Hewlett Packard Enterprise's 1.15X, but lower than Arista Networks' 13.43X.

CSCO Valuation

Cisco Rides on Strong Portfolio & AI Demand

Cisco Systems' long-term prospects remain promising, driven by its diversified networking, security, observability and collaboration portfolio, alongside rising investments in AI infrastructure.

Strong AI infrastructure demand remains a key growth catalyst. The company expects AI infrastructure revenues from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027, supported by growing demand and market share gains. Increasing adoption of its Silicon One P200 and G200 systems, alongside expanding opportunities in scale-out and scale-across networking, should further strengthen its growth trajectory.

Cisco Systems' security and observability businesses offer substantial growth opportunities as enterprises increasingly prioritize protection against AI-related cyber threats. The integration of Splunk with Cisco Systems security portfolio, alongside growing adoption of Hypershield, AI Defense and Secure Access, should support cross-selling opportunities and recurring revenue growth. Management expects security and observability revenues to grow at a high-single-digit rate in fiscal 2027.

Conclusion

Cisco Systems' first-quarter fiscal 2027 results are likely to reflect strong AI infrastructure momentum, robust networking demand and an expanding security portfolio. Rising hyperscaler investments, growing adoption of Silicon One and improving Splunk momentum further strengthen its growth prospects. These factors justify its premium valuation.

news.Title: APPS Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Ad Growth, Guidance Up
news.Content:
Digital Turbine APPS reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, up 20% from 15 cents in the year-ago quarter. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 12.5%.

Net revenues totaled $178.68 million, increasing 27.3% year over year and surpassing the consensus estimate by 7.24%. Strength across the On Device Solutions and App Growth Platform segments, supported by AI-driven advertising improvements, fueled growth. Adjusted EBITDA increased 46% year over year.

APPS' Q2 Revenue Growth Drivers

Digital Turbine's On Device Solutions segment generated $115.6 million in net revenues before intercompany eliminations, up 20% year over year. International revenues grew approximately 50%, supported by higher device volumes and improved revenue per device despite smartphone supply-chain headwinds.

App Growth Platform revenues reached $63.5 million, increasing 42% year over year. This marked the segment's fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and third consecutive quarter of more than 40% growth. DT Exchange revenues increased 42%, while the brand business grew 45%, reflecting stronger advertiser demand and AI-powered optimization.

Digital Turbine, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Digital Turbine, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Digital Turbine, Inc. Quote

Digital Turbine's AI Initiatives Gain Traction

Management highlighted improving advertising performance through its first-party data and AI-powered targeting capabilities. Higher advertiser returns on ad spending supported stronger pricing and fill rates, particularly across premium advertising placements.

The company also benefited from increasing demand for mobile-app advertising and diversification beyond gaming. Nearly 40% of advertiser spending on DT Exchange came from non-gaming partners. Digital Turbine continues expanding its publisher network, particularly across Asia Pacific, while attracting AI-focused applications seeking monetization opportunities.

APPS' Q2 Operating Details

The non-GAAP gross margin contracted 400 basis points (bps) year over year to 43%.

Sales and marketing expenses, as a percentage of revenues, declined to 8.1% from 10.3% in the year-ago quarter. General and administrative expenses decreased to 18.3% of revenues from 24.3%, while product development expenses declined to 5.6% from 7.8%.

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased to $39.8 million from $27.2 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded approximately 290 bps to 22.3%, reflecting improved operating leverage and expense discipline.

Digital Turbine reported GAAP operating income of $20.3 million compared with $6.5 million in the year-ago quarter. GAAP net income reached $10.3 million against a net loss of $21.4 million a year earlier.

Story Continues

Digital Turbine's Cash Flow and Balance Sheet

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $51.62 million compared with $43.21 million at the end of the preceding quarter.

Cash flow from operating activities was $18.84 million compared with $14.46 million in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP free cash flow increased to $10.46 million from $7.03 million, reflecting improved cash generation despite continued investments in the business.

Total debt, net of issuance costs and discounts, stood at approximately $353.61 million. Management highlighted continued deleveraging, with the net leverage ratio improving to approximately 2.3 times from more than 4 times a year earlier.

APPS Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue Guidance

For fiscal 2027, Digital Turbine now expects revenues between $670 million and $690 million, up from the previously guided range of $650 million to $670 million. The company reaffirmed its adjusted EBITDA guidance of $145 million to $155 million.

Management attributed the improved revenue outlook to sustained momentum in AI-driven advertising, stronger performance across its platforms and increased partner adoption. The company plans additional investments in data science, machine learning and AI infrastructure during the second half of fiscal 2027 to support future growth.

Digital Turbine's Expanding Global Opportunities

International expansion remains a key priority. Management expects initial revenues from its Orange partnership in the current quarter and anticipates launching services with another Tier 1 European telecommunications operator during fiscal 2027. These partnerships are expected to contribute more meaningfully to growth in fiscal 2028.

Digital Turbine is also expanding its Ignite platform beyond traditional app distribution into AI agents, e-commerce, lock-screen services and other content offerings. Management expects its expanding device footprint and AI-enabled advertising capabilities to support continued revenue growth, while incremental investments could moderate near-term profitability gains.

APPS's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

Digital Turbine currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector include Cisco Systems CSCO, Analog Devices ADI and NVIDIA NVDA. Each stock presently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Cisco Systems shares have gained 28.1% year to date. Cisco Systems is set to report first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12.

Shares of Analog Devices have risen 45.5% year to date. Analog Devices is set to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 24.

NVIDIA shares have lost 4.2% year to date. NVIDIA is set to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 17.

news.Title: 5 AI Stock Picks and Performance of Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller
news.Content:
Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller has been bullish on AI since before ChatGPT launched. He is one of the most closely followed macro investors on Wall Street. He averaged about 30% a year at Duquesne Capital with no losing year, and his 1992 bet against the British pound made more than $1 billion.

Druckenmiller's AI Stock Picks Take a Beating

The AI trade has taken a turn for the worse since the end of the second quarter. Nine of Stanley Druckenmiller's 10 AI stock picks on this list have declined since June 30, with the stocks losing an average of 27.8% on an equal-weight basis through November 9, compared with a gain of about 0.8% for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). We have included each stock's performance since June 30 in the list below. But did Druckenmiller get out before the crash? We could find out in just a few days, when his family office is expected to disclose its third-quarter holdings. The filing will reveal whether he sold or reduced positions before the latest AI selloff, or held on to stocks that subsequently suffered steep losses.
